bullets.title: JPMorgan turns tactically cautious; September seasonality and Fed live risk cited
bullets.body: JPMorgan's trading desk shifted to a tactically cautious/neutral stance, citing a live Fed in September (market pricing ~38-65bp of tightening post-Warsh Jackson Hole comments), choppy positioning, credit spread widening risk post-Labor Day, and momentum factor down 21-34% from June ATH — well outside the typical 10-15% drawdown range. September is historically the worst month for QQQs (10yr avg -1.6%), though post-midterm election seasonality is bullish (+5-15% at various tenors).

bullets.title: Hormuz tanker strikes drive WTI +2.4% to ~$88; geopolitical premium embedding in rates
bullets.body: Two oil supertankers struck by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz, sending Oct WTI up ~$2.07 (+2.41%) to $87.83 and Brent above $90. Jefferies frames this as an inflation/fiscal problem rather than a growth shock: higher delivered energy costs feed sticky inflation constraining Fed flexibility, while ~$9-10tn in Treasury refinancing due in the next 12 months makes elevated yields existential. Trump was separately reported to be weighing limited strikes on Iran.

bullets.title: Global bond yields at multi-decade highs; UK Gilt +9bp, JGB hits 30-year high
bullets.body: Sovereign yields are breaking out globally: UK 30-yr Gilt hit 5.873% (+9.3bp, a two-standard-deviation move), Japanese 2yr JGB up 6.7bp to 1.793% (three-sigma move) with the 10yr approaching 3% for the first time in 30 years. Hedgeye frames this as Global Quad3 Stagflation persisting into Q3, keeping TLT/ZROZ as core shorts; UST 10yr yield broke above the 4.74% cycle high to ~4.80%, and the 30-yr has been above 5% for the longest stretch since 2006.

bullets.title: Tech/semis slide 2-4% pre-market; NOW, CRWV, MRVL, INTC lead declines
bullets.body: Broad tech and semiconductor names are under 2-4% premarket pressure despite AI compute demand tailwinds: NOW -3.0%, CRWV -3.1%, MRVL -3.4%, INTC -2.8%, AAOI -3.7%, AXTI -4.2%, IONQ -2.7%. S&P futures are mixed across sources (range of -0.5% to +0.6% cited depending on timing) while Nasdaq futures are down roughly 1%. NVDA and MSFT contributed ~50% of the S&P's 250bp August gain.

bullets.title: Anthropic/$35B Lambda deal and NVDA-MediaTek $3.5B investment anchor AI capex narrative
bullets.body: Anthropic signed a $35B cloud-computing deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda; Nvidia will supply chips and hold the Texas data center lease. Separately, Nvidia is investing $3.5B in MediaTek via convertible bonds for custom AI chip co-development (TPUv8/v9 ASIC work), NVLink Fusion, PC AI, and automotive partnerships. AI datacenter capex is forecast to reach $3T by 2030; HBM demand is growing 200%+ YoY vs. supply ~20%, with the bottleneck expected to persist through 2030.

bullets.title: UBS raises 2027/28 WFE forecasts to $225B/$275B; 2029 biased above $300B
bullets.body: UBS raised its wafer fab equipment spending forecasts from $198B/$248B to $225B/$275B for 2027/2028, with 2029 expected to eclipse $300B. 2027 growth of ~43% YoY is driven by DRAM +60%, NAND +30%, and foundry/logic +34%. Equipment ASPs are rising 5-10% cumulatively through 2028, adding $10-30B that is not yet reflected in Street consensus. SpaceX Terafab is projected at ~$11B WFE spend in 2028, potentially rivaling TSMC/Intel within 4-5 years.

bullets.title: SB Energy IPO filed; NVDA commits $1.5B equity stake in AI data center buildout
bullets.body: SB Energy (ticker SBE) filed its S-1 on Nasdaq, operating 8.8 GW-IT of data center capacity with a $439B backlog and SoftBank/OpenAI as strategic partners. Nvidia contractually committed to purchase $1.5B of non-voting equity at IPO price and acts as residual value guarantor at the PORTS-Pike Ohio campus (4.25 IT-GW for OpenAI, coming online 2028). 6-month revenue was $138.7M vs $83.3M YoY.

bullets.title: Fed: Warsh Jackson Hole comments keep September hike live; NFP Friday is binary
bullets.body: Markets are pricing ~38-65bp of Fed tightening in 2026 following Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole R-star commentary. JPM's Feroli forecasts Friday NFP at 50k (vs. Street 55k), 4.1% unemployment; a 30-70k print is the 'Goldilocks' range for markets. Wolfe notes the bar for action is low — core PCE above 0.25% MoM would meaningfully raise odds of a move; August core CPI is forecast at 0.19% MoM (in-line).

bullets.title: Euro area core inflation ticks down to 2.41%; energy prices up 14.3% YoY keep headline elevated
bullets.body: Euro area August headline CPI rose to 3.26% YoY driven by energy (+14.3% YoY), while core edged down 7bp to 2.41% YoY with services down 24bp to 3.05%. JPMorgan raised its Brent assumption to $90/bbl in September, declining to $80 by year-end. Core inflation is forecast to rise toward 2.6% at start of 2027 before gradually declining.

bullets.title: Hedgeye Quad3 framework: short duration, short utilities; buy gold on dips
bullets.body: Hedgeye maintains Global Quad3 Stagflation as the aggregate G20 regime for Q3, potentially shifting to Quad2 in Q4. Core positioning: short TLT, ZROZ, LQD, XLU; cover some shorts as yields approach risk-range tops; buy gold and GDX on corrections. SPX bullish risk range is 7,627-7,748; VIX range 14.03-16.28; positive dealer gamma suggests buying weakness and fading strength near-term.

bullets.title: Software bounced 47% off April lows on positioning, not fundamentals; re-rating requires AI acceleration
bullets.body: Citi notes the IGV/software bounce was driven by extreme short covering and cross-asset unwinds rather than fundamental improvement — short interest as a % of float has surpassed both the 2016 SaaS correction and 2008 GFC peaks. Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales with IGV -2.2% YTD vs. S&P +12.9%. Fewer than 50% of software companies are expected to accelerate growth; durable re-rating requires tangible AI-driven fundamental acceleration.

bullets.title: Agentic inference reshaping AI chip architectures from compute-bound to memory-bandwidth-bound
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Hot Chips takeaway: agentic inference is shifting AI architecture priorities from compute to memory bandwidth, with custom ASICs trending toward parity with merchant GPUs. AVGO appears across Google TPU, Jalapeño, Meta MTIA, and SambaNova RDU platforms. OpenAI's Jalapeño chip removes L2 cache to cut inference latency and was developed in a 16-month cycle alongside Broadcom.

bullets.title: FTC sues Amazon for $20B+ in alleged ad price manipulation; Citi maintains Buy, sees lawsuit as overblown
bullets.body: The FTC and 22+ states filed suit alleging Amazon overcharged ~1.2M advertisers by $20B+ via undisclosed reserve-pricing mechanisms since 2019. Amazon stock fell ~2.5% to ~$259. Citi reiterates Buy at $350 PT, noting CPCs remained flat inflation-adjusted 2019-2024 while conversion rates rose 24%+, and that AWS AI tailwinds (2M+ NVDA GPUs deploying 2027-28) support the investment case. A third separate FTC case is also being filed in Seattle.

bullets.title: JPMorgan global equity strategy remains bullish; non-US stocks outperforming US for second year
bullets.body: JPMorgan stays bullish into year-end on global equities (+15% YTD), citing continued earnings delivery and EPS revisions turning outright positive in all regions. Eurozone PMIs are up three months in a row; cyclical sectors (Mining, Banks, Capital Goods, Semis) expected to rally. Non-US stocks are outperforming the US for the second consecutive year; bond yield increases are viewed as unlikely to derail stocks as inflation expectations remain anchored.

bullets.title: Data center NIMBYism spreading; 9 states with pending moratoriums, but EQIX/DLR entitled projects insulated
bullets.body: Mizuho flags growing state-level data center restrictions with NY's state-wide moratorium and 20+ states with restrictive legislation. However, EQIX and DLR's under-construction projects are already entitled with grid connections secured; land banks face some risk. Mizuho rates both Outperform: EQIX at $1,275 PT (22% upside), DLR at $223 PT (20% upside). Morgan Stanley separately flags data center pushback as a wedge issue in midterm election races.

bullets.title: Macau August GGR -1% YoY at MOP21.9B, slight miss; late-month deceleration to MOP655m/day
bullets.body: Macau August GGR came in at MOP21.9B (-1.2% YoY, +8% MoM), missing consensus of MOP722m/day; the last 8 days averaged only MOP655m/day vs. MOP724m/day in the first 23 days. VIP remains deeply depressed at 54% of 2019 levels while mass is at ~119% recovery. The sector trades at 8.6x 2026E EV/EBITDA, 0.6 standard deviations below the 2023 average. JPM's pecking order: Galaxy > Wynn > Sands > MGM/MLCO.

bullets.title: Walmart's $3B tariff-refund price investment equals ~60% of Kroger's entire EBIT; Citi opens downside watch
bullets.body: Walmart is investing ~$3B from tariff refunds into food/grocery price cuts to gain market share, with management expecting vendors to sustain investments beyond 3Q. Citi cuts Kroger FY26 EPS to $5.05 from $5.22 and PT to $57 from $61, anticipates management will guide comps down from +1-2% to +1-1.5% at the September 11 earnings print. KR foot traffic decelerated to +0.4% in 2Q vs. +1.7% in 1Q.

bullets.title: US-Canada trade talks collapse; 50% tit-for-tat tariffs loom; US-China summit path open
bullets.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent blamed his Canadian counterpart for the breakdown in trade talks, with 50% retaliatory tariffs now on the table. Separately, the US and China are discussing lower tariffs on 'non-sensitive' products ahead of a Trump-Xi summit. South Korea export growth accelerated ~69% in August on AI-driven chip demand, and China's manufacturing PMI firmed in August.

bullets.title: META settles mental health lawsuit for ~$18B; Morgan Stanley upgrades to OW at $775 PT
bullets.body: Meta settled state AG mental health lawsuits for ~$18B (10 years), with a $10B legal accrual expected in 3Q; product changes for teen safety are expected to have immaterial revenue impact (teens <1% of revenue). Morgan Stanley upgrades to Overweight with $775 PT, noting META trades at 16x forward EPS (~25% below long-term average and ~45% below 2025 peak), with a pipeline of MetaAI, agentic ad tools, subscriptions, and APIs potentially worth $10+ in EPS.

bullets.title: SMCI guides FY27 revenue $65-72B (+75% YoY); ~70% AI, 30% CPU-based
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer provided FY27 guidance of $65-72B in revenue (+75% YoY), with roughly 70% of that being pure AI server deployments and 30% CPU-based. Texas and Pennsylvania governors tightened data center regulatory requirements in August. DELL and HPE are separately flagged as poised to benefit from continued GPU and CPU server strength in neoclouds.
